en: Live rounds are used during training exercises.
note: уче́ния are military training exercises; "at the exercises" reads as a gym class.
English puts the force on the verb, not an adverb of pain — "hit his head painfully" is not said.
«ва́жно» here is putting on airs, which "importantly" does not convey — it reads as "notably".

en: Suddenly, it began to rain heavily.
note: English makes rain the verb, not the subject of "began".
The proposal was an over-translation fix and still invents a recipient: «рассказа́ли» names no "me".

en: The empire broke up into parts.
note: "Broke apart into pieces" says the same thing twice.

en: Security guards are standing at the gate.
note: Abstract "security" does not stand anywhere; the guards do.

en: Anything is possible if you really want it.
note: "Given the desire" is a calque of «при жела́нии»; English uses a conditional clause.
The idiomatic rendering of «У меня́ возника́ет вопро́с»; the literal one is not English.
Restores the natural reading the rewrite demoted to an alternate — «си́лы» is the speaker's own strength, and it fades rather than disappears.

ru: В тишине́ разда́лся бы любо́й шо́рох.
en: In the silence, any rustle would be clearly audible.
note: A rustle cannot ring out; «разда́ться» here is about being heard, not about volume.

en: The door will soon slam in the wind.
note: English says a door slams *in* the wind, not *from* it.
